rules.name: Syntax error
rules.description: The parser could not read the source code.

rules.name: Unused suppression
rules.description: An lsp-ignore comment suppresses no finding and can be removed.
rules.bad:
// lsp-ignore: empty-except
X := 1;

rules.name: Unknown rule id
rules.description: An lsp-ignore comment names a rule id that does not exist, so it suppresses nothing. The message suggests the most similar known id (typo); such a comment is not also reported as unused-suppression.
rules.bad:
// lsp-ignore: empty-exept
try X; except end;
rules.good:
// lsp-ignore: empty-except
try X; except end;

rules.name: Bidirectional control character
rules.description: Bidirectional control characters can make code display differently from how it compiles (Trojan Source); also in form files. Direction marks in RTL text only with low confidence.
rules.bad: if IsAdmin then { U+202E } begin
rules.good: if IsAdmin then begin

rules.name: Invisible character
rules.description: Invisible or zero-width characters in the source code and form files; medium confidence in strings and comments.
rules.bad: Count{U+200B} := 0;
rules.good: Count := 0;

rules.name: Control character
rules.description: NUL or control characters or invalid UTF-8 bytes in the source code and the form file; invalid bytes with exact line and column.

rules.name: Confusable identifier
rules.description: Identifiers that mix scripts or contain non-ASCII characters can be confused with others.
rules.bad: var Pаssword: string; { Cyrillic 'а' }
rules.good: var Password: string;

rules.name: Forbidden uses
rules.description: A uses entry violates a layer rule configured under "layers" in atlas.json, e.g. *.Common.* must not use Vcl.*.

options.name: layers
options.description: Layer rules: [{"from": glob, "deny": [globs], "allow": [globs]}].

rules.name: Import violates the role matrix
rules.description: A uses entry violates the import matrix of the role concept (output artefact, feature, role: Contract, Internals, Providers, Adapters, Composition, Hosting). Off by default; switch it on in atlas.json with the option "prefixes". Approved exceptions go to "allow" as "Source -> Target" globs.

options.name: prefixes
options.description: Prefixes of the output artefacts, e.g. "Atlas.Common"; without them the rule reports nothing.

options.name: hostRoles
options.description: First name segments of host units without prefix.

options.name: allow
options.description: Approved exceptions "Source -> Target" (both globs).

rules.name: Class in a contract unit
rules.description: A contract unit declares a class in its interface section. Contracts hold only records, interfaces, enumerations and exceptions. Off by default; switch it on in atlas.json with the option "prefixes". Approved exceptions go to "allow" as "Unit.Type" globs.

options.name: prefixes
options.description: Prefixes of the output artefacts, e.g. "Atlas.Common".

options.name: allow
options.description: Approved exceptions "Unit.Type" as glob.

rules.name: VCL access from a thread
rules.description: TThread.Execute, TThread.CreateAnonymousThread or TTask accesses the VCL (Application, Screen, ShowMessage, MessageDlg …) outside Synchronize or Queue. The VCL is not thread-safe.

rules.name: Lock without try/finally
rules.description: A lock (TCriticalSection.Enter/Acquire, TMonitor.Enter, BeginRead/BeginWrite, TSpinLock.Enter, TMutex.Acquire, EnterCriticalSection or a pair from the lockPairs option) is not directly followed by try/finally releasing it. An exception leaves the lock held.

options.name: lockPairs
options.description: Additional lock pairs as [["Lock", "Release"]].

rules.name: Thread used after start with FreeOnTerminate
rules.description: A thread with FreeOnTerminate := True may free itself as soon as it is started; using the variable afterwards can access a freed object.

rules.name: Free on a thread with FreeOnTerminate
rules.description: Free on a thread with FreeOnTerminate := True frees it twice.
rules.good:
T.FreeOnTerminate := True;
T.Start;

rules.name: Synchronize in thread destructor
rules.description: Synchronize in the destructor of a TThread descendant (or a method it calls) deadlocks: the main thread waits in WaitFor while the thread waits for Synchronize.

rules.name: Deprecated TThread.Resume/Suspend
rules.description: TThread.Resume and Suspend are deprecated. Start a created thread with Start; Suspend has no safe replacement, wait with an event instead.
rules.bad: FWorker.Resume;
rules.good: FWorker.Start;

rules.name: Function result possibly not set
rules.description: A path through the function ends without assigning Result. The caller then reads an undefined value.

rules.name: Variable possibly uninitialized
rules.description: A local variable is read on a path where it was never assigned.

rules.name: Unreachable code
rules.description: A statement after Exit, raise, Abort, Halt, Break, Continue or goto is never executed. Usually a leftover or a misplaced jump. Only the first statement of an unreachable section is reported.

rules.name: Unused local variable
rules.description: A local variable is declared but never used. Like compiler hint H2164, but while typing.

options.name: ignore
options.description: Name patterns that are never reported (* and ?).

rules.name: Unused parameter
rules.description: A parameter is never used in the routine body. Overridden and virtual methods, event handlers, published methods, interface implementations and callbacks are exempt.

options.name: ignore
options.description: Name patterns that are never reported (* and ?).

rules.name: Value assigned is never used
rules.description: A value assigned to a local variable is overwritten or the routine ends before it is read. Like compiler hint H2077.

options.name: ignore
options.description: Name patterns that are never reported (* and ?).

rules.name: Declared but not implemented
rules.description: A method is declared in a class, record or object but has no body in the implementation section. The compiler reports this only when compiling (E2065). A body of the same name with a different header is reported by signature-mismatch instead.

rules.name: Implemented but not declared
rules.description: A method body TFoo.Bar has no declaration of that name in the type. A declaration of the same name with a different header is reported by signature-mismatch instead.

rules.name: Destroy without override
rules.description: A destructor Destroy is declared without override. Free calls TObject.Destroy, so this destructor never runs.

rules.name: Setter or getter calls itself
rules.description: A setter assigns to its own property (Name := Value in SetName) or a getter reads it (Result := Name in GetName). The accessor calls itself endlessly and ends in a stack overflow at run time; the compiler stays silent. Quick fix: use the field instead (the field from the property declaration, otherwise F plus the name, if the class has it). Formerly recursive-property-accessor; settings and suppressions with the old ID still apply.

rules.name: Component constructor without override
rules.description: A TComponent descendant declares constructor Create(AOwner: TComponent) without override. Components created from a form file are built through the virtual constructor and skip this one.

rules.name: Method hides virtual method
rules.description: A method has the same name as a virtual method of an ancestor but neither overrides nor reintroduces it (compiler warning W1010).

rules.name: virtual instead of override
rules.description: A descendant declares a method virtual although the ancestor already has a virtual method with the same signature; this starts a new chain instead of overriding.

rules.name: Captured loop variable
rules.description: An anonymous method passed to a deferred API (TThread.Queue, TTask.Run, ...) captures a variable that changes before it runs, such as a for-in loop variable. Delphi captures the variable, not its value.
rules.bad:
for S in List do
  TThread.Queue(nil, procedure begin Memo1.Lines.Add(S); end);

options.name: deferredApis
options.description: Additional deferred APIs (besides TThread.Queue, TTask.Run and others).

rules.name: Component method without inherited
rules.description: An overridden Loaded, CreateParams, CreateWnd, Notification, SetParent, Destroy or Paint of a component does not call inherited, so the VCL skips its own work there. For Paint the confidence is low, because TCustomControl.Paint only draws the design-time frame.

rules.name: default does not match constructor
rules.description: A property declares a default value, but the constructor sets its field to a different literal. The streaming system does not store values equal to default, so the property is loaded wrongly from the DFM.

rules.name: Component reference without FreeNotification
rules.description: A component property refers to another component, but its setter does not call FreeNotification. When the other component is freed, a dangling pointer remains. Subcomponents created in the constructor are ignored.

rules.name: Setter without Invalidate
rules.description: A property setter changes a field that Paint reads, but does not call Invalidate (or Repaint, Refresh, Changed). The control keeps showing the old state.

rules.name: Fixed pixel values
rules.description: Paint or Resize uses fixed pixel values that are too small above 96 dpi. Values passed through ScaleValue or MulDiv, 0, 1 and -1, and factors of multiplications and divisions are not reported.
rules.bad: Canvas.FillRect(Rect(0, 0, 16, 16));
rules.good: Canvas.FillRect(Rect(0, 0, ScaleValue(16), ScaleValue(16)));

rules.name: Hardcoded color in Paint
rules.description: Paint uses an RGB literal, a $00BBGGRR constant or a TColor cast. Such colors ignore VCL styles; system colors like clBtnFace are fine.
rules.bad: Canvas.Brush.Color := $00FF8000;
rules.good: Canvas.Brush.Color := StyleServices.GetSystemColor(clHighlight);

rules.name: Form field without object
rules.description: A published component field of the form class has no object in the .dfm/.fmx next to the unit. After loading, the field stays nil. Fields outside published are not checked.
rules.bad: Edit1: TEdit;  // object Edit1 was deleted from the form
rules.good: // remove the field or restore the object

rules.name: Form object without field
rules.description: An object of the form file has no field in the form class. Inherited objects, objects inside inline frames, unnamed components and collection items are skipped. The fix adds the field.
rules.bad: object Button2: TButton  // no Button2 in TForm1
rules.good: Button2: TButton;

rules.name: Form field type differs from object
rules.description: The field type differs from the class of the object in the form file. Without source for the class in the form file, nothing is compared. The fix changes the field type.
rules.bad: Edit1: TEdit;  // object Edit1: TMaskEdit
rules.good: Edit1: TMaskEdit;

rules.name: Command injection
rules.description: ShellExecute, ShellExecuteEx, CreateProcess or WinExec receives an argument built with +, Format or Concat from non-constant values. Input could inject further commands. Without data flow analysis only this simple pattern is found (medium confidence).
rules.bad: ShellExecute(0, 'open', PChar('cmd /c ' + Edit1.Text), nil, nil, SW_SHOW);
rules.good: ShellExecute(0, 'open', 'tool.exe', PChar(QuotedArgument), nil, SW_SHOW);  // validated

rules.name: Path traversal
rules.description: A file access (TFileStream.Create, LoadFromFile, AssignFile, TFile.*) uses a path from input data (Text, ParamStr, Request) without TPath.GetFullPath check. Experimental until data flow analysis is available.
rules.bad: List.LoadFromFile('C:\Data\' + Edit1.Text);
rules.good: Path := TPath.GetFullPath(TPath.Combine(Root, Edit1.Text));  // then check it starts with Root

rules.name: Weak cryptography
rules.description: MD5, SHA-1, DES or RC4 is used. For checksums this is fine; for passwords and signatures it is not. Low confidence, medium when the statement mentions a password, secret or signature.
rules.bad: Stored := THashSHA1.GetHashString(PasswordText);
rules.good: Stored := THashSHA2.GetHashString(Salt + PasswordText);

rules.name: TLS certificate check disabled
rules.description: Indy SSLOptions.VerifyMode := [], an OnVerifyPeer handler that always returns True, or a ValidateServerCertificate handler that sets Accepted := True without a check.
rules.bad: IdSSL.SSLOptions.VerifyMode := [];
rules.good: IdSSL.SSLOptions.VerifyMode := [sslvrfPeer];

rules.name: Unencrypted http:// URL
rules.description: A string contains an http:// URL. XML namespaces and schema URIs, comments and localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] are skipped. The fix replaces http:// with https://.
rules.bad: Client.Get('http://api.example.com/data');
rules.good: Client.Get('https://api.example.com/data');

rules.name: Random for security values
rules.description: Random is assigned to a token, password, salt, nonce or key. Random is predictable; use a cryptographic random generator. Missing Randomize is a separate topic (#153).
rules.bad: Token := IntToStr(Random(MaxInt));
rules.good: Token := TNetEncoding.Base64URL.EncodeBytesToString(CryptoRandomBytes(32));

rules.name: Circular master-detail or data source link
rules.description: MasterSource/DataSource links in the form file form a cycle (tblA → dsB → tblB → dsA → tblA). Opening the datasets recurses or never shows consistent data.
rules.bad: tblA.MasterSource = dsB; tblB.MasterSource = dsA
rules.good: tblB.MasterSource = dsA  // tblA has no master

rules.name: Master-detail without MasterFields
rules.description: A dataset has MasterSource but no MasterFields. The detail is not filtered and shows all records.
rules.bad: MasterSource = dsKunden
rules.good: MasterSource = dsKunden; MasterFields = 'KundenID'

rules.name: Required field without visible input control
rules.description: A persistent field with Required = True is bound to no visible data-aware control (a grid without DataField counts for all fields). The user cannot fill it and posting fails.
rules.bad: tblKundenName: Required = True, no TDBEdit for Name
rules.good: edName: TDBEdit; DataSource = dsKunden; DataField = 'Name'

rules.name: Data-aware control does not fit the field type
rules.description: The control does not suit the persistent field, e.g. TDBEdit on a TBooleanField or blob field, TDBImage on a non-graphic field.
rules.bad: edAktiv: TDBEdit; DataField = 'Aktiv'  // TBooleanField
rules.good: cbAktiv: TDBCheckBox; DataField = 'Aktiv'

rules.name: Two controls bound to the same field
rules.description: Two input controls use the same DataSource and DataField. Usually a copy-and-paste error. Display controls (TDBText, TDBImage) are ignored.
rules.bad: ed1, ed2: DataSource = dsA; DataField = 'Name'
rules.good: ed1: DataField = 'Name'; ed2: DataField = 'Vorname'

rules.name: Component property violates a property rule
rules.description: A component property in the form file does not meet a rule from dfmPropertyRules in atlas.json (class, property, condition, value). A property that is not stored counts with its default value; objects of the ancestor form are only reported where this form sets the value itself. The quick fix sets the value in the form file (fix: auto also with source.fixAll); the command "Apply property rules" corrects one form, the project or the group with a preview.
rules.bad:
// dfmPropertyRules: TLabel.Transparent = True
object Label1: TLabel
  Caption = 'Name'
end
rules.good:
object Label1: TLabel
  Caption = 'Name'
  Transparent = True
end

rules.name: Access to controls of another form
rules.description: Code accesses a field of a form or frame from another unit through its global variable (Form2.Edit1.Text). This couples the units tightly; use a method or property of the form.
rules.bad: Form2.Edit1.Text := 'x';
rules.good: Form2.Kundenname := 'x';

rules.name: SQL text built from values (SQL injection)
rules.description: SQL.Text, SQL.Add, CommandText, ExecSQL or Open receives text built with + or Format from non-constant values. User input could inject SQL. Use parameters (:Name, ParamByName). Constants, resourcestrings, IntToStr and QuotedStr are not reported; user input (TEdit.Text, TMemo.Lines) raises the confidence to high.
rules.bad: Q.SQL.Text := 'select * from K where N = ''' + Edit1.Text + '''';
rules.good:
Q.SQL.Text := 'select * from K where N = :N';
Q.ParamByName('N').AsString := Edit1.Text;

rules.name: Quick command not executed
rules.description: A line starting with /name was not executed and stays in the code: the command is unknown, switched off (slashCommands.disabled) or does not fit at this place. The message names the reason. "/ignore rule" is also reported when that rule finds nothing in the line below.
rules.bad: /gibtsnicht X
rules.good: /uses System.Classes

rules.name: Empty except block
rules.description: An except block without statements swallows every exception. A block that contains only a comment counts as deliberate and is not reported.

rules.name: Interface without GUID
rules.description: An interface declares no GUID. Supports, as and QueryInterface need one. The confidence is high when the interface is used with them in the same file, otherwise low. The quick fix inserts a new GUID.

rules.name: Two interfaces with the same GUID
rules.description: Two interfaces in the file declare the same GUID, usually after copying a declaration. Supports and as then mix them up. The quick fix generates a new GUID.

rules.name: File header missing or different
rules.description: The file does not start with the header from the rule option "template". Off by default; switch it on in atlas.json with a template. The quick fix inserts the header.
rules.bad: unit Tools;
rules.good:
// Copyright (c) Example GmbH
unit Tools;

options.name: template
options.description: Expected file header; placeholders as documented.

rules.name: Text in code instead of resourcestring
rules.description: A string literal with words for people stands in a statement. Move it to a resourcestring so it can be translated. Off by default, low confidence.
rules.bad: ShowMessage('File not found');

rules.name: Assignment to itself
rules.description: A variable, field or property is assigned to itself. Usually a different value was meant, for example a parameter or another field. If a parameter or local variable hides a field of the same name (Name := Name), Atlas offers Self.Name := Name as the fix.
rules.bad: FName := FName;
rules.good: FName := AName;

rules.name: for loop counts down with to
rules.description: The loop starts at the upper bound (High, Count - 1) and ends at the lower one, but uses to. It never runs; downto was meant.
rules.bad:
for I := High(A) to Low(A) do
  Save(A[I]);
rules.good:
for I := High(A) downto Low(A) do
  Save(A[I]);

rules.name: Exception created but not raised
rules.description: An exception object is created as a statement on its own. Without raise nothing happens and the object leaks.
rules.bad:
if X = nil then
  EArgumentException.Create('X missing');
rules.good:
if X = nil then
  raise EArgumentException.Create('X missing');

rules.name: Assert with side effect
rules.description: The argument of Assert changes data (Inc, Dec, a Try… function with an out parameter or a method from the option mutatingMethods). With {$C-} the compiler removes the whole call including the side effect.
rules.bad: Assert(List.Remove(X) >= 0);
rules.good:
Index := List.Remove(X);
Assert(Index >= 0);

options.name: mutatingMethods
options.description: Methods that change their object.

rules.name: IfThen evaluates both branches
rules.description: IfThen is a function: both branches are evaluated before the call. A nil access or a function call in the branch that is not chosen still happens. High confidence when a branch dereferences a name checked in the condition, medium for a function call.
rules.bad: S := IfThen(Assigned(X), X.Name, '');
rules.good: if Assigned(X) then S := X.Name else S := '';

rules.name: Random without Randomize
rules.description: Random is used, but the unit never calls Randomize, so every start yields the same sequence. Randomize often sits in the .dpr, so the rule is off by default and has low confidence.
rules.bad: Dice := Random(6) + 1;

rules.name: Int32 multiplication assigned to Int64
rules.description: Both operands have at most 32 bits, so the product is computed in 32 bits and overflows before it is assigned to the Int64 variable. Cast one operand to Int64.
rules.bad: Total := Width * Height; // Total: Int64; Width, Height: Integer
rules.good: Total := Int64(Width) * Height;

rules.name: SizeOf of a pointer in Move or FillChar
rules.description: SizeOf of a pointer, string or dynamic array is the size of the reference (4 or 8 bytes), not of the data. Move and FillChar then copy or clear too little.
rules.bad: FillChar(Buffer[0], SizeOf(Buffer), 0); // Buffer: TBytes
rules.good: FillChar(Buffer[0], Length(Buffer) * SizeOf(Buffer[0]), 0);

rules.name: Char cast to PChar
rules.description: PChar(C) with a Char variable turns the character code into an address. A string was meant.
rules.bad: ShowMessage(PChar(C)); // C: Char
rules.good: ShowMessage(PChar(string(C)));

rules.name: Floating-point comparison with = or <>
rules.description: Floating-point values are rarely exactly equal after calculations. Compare with SameValue from System.Math and a tolerance. Comparisons with 0 are not reported.
rules.bad: if Total = Expected then
rules.good: if SameValue(Total, Expected) then

rules.name: Constructor called on an instance
rules.description: Create is called on a variable instead of the class. That does not create a new object; with an unassigned variable it crashes. Class references (class of …) are not reported.
rules.bad: List.Create; // List: TStringList
rules.good: List := TStringList.Create;

rules.name: Formatting depends on the locale
rules.description: Format with %f, %n, %m, %g or %e and functions like FloatToStr, StrToFloat or DateToStr without a TFormatSettings parameter use the user's locale (decimal separator, date format). For files, protocols and logs pass fixed TFormatSettings. Format('%d', …) is not reported.
rules.bad: Line := Format('%.2f', [Amount]);
rules.good: Line := Format('%.2f', [Amount], TFormatSettings.Invariant);

rules.name: Generic exception raised
rules.description: Raising the base class Exception prevents callers from handling the error specifically. Declare a dedicated exception class.
rules.bad: raise Exception.Create('Customer missing');
rules.good: raise ECustomerMissing.Create('Customer missing');

rules.name: Catch-all handler without re-raise
rules.description: A handler for Exception that neither re-raises nor ends the program swallows every error, including programming errors. Off by default; intended for library code.

rules.name: Exception object freed manually
rules.description: The RTL frees an exception object after its handler or after raise. Freeing it manually causes a double free.
rules.bad:
on E: Exception do
  E.Free;
rules.good:
on E: Exception do
  Log(E.Message);

rules.name: String concatenation in a loop
rules.description: A string variable is extended step by step inside a loop. Delphi usually grows strings in place, so this is reported only with low confidence and is off by default; for many iterations TStringBuilder is faster.
rules.bad:
for I := 1 to 10000 do
  S := S + IntToStr(I);

rules.name: Expensive call in a loop condition
rules.description: The condition of while and until is evaluated on every iteration. Calls like Trim, Format or FileExists and properties like Lines.Text there are recomputed each time; compute them once before the loop. Bounds of for loops are evaluated only once and are not reported. Off by default.
rules.bad:
while I < Length(Trim(Memo.Lines.Text)) do
  Inc(I);

rules.name: Adding items in a loop without BeginUpdate
rules.description: Items.Add, Lines.Add and similar calls in a loop repaint the control on every call. Wrap the loop in BeginUpdate and try … finally EndUpdate. Off by default.
rules.bad:
for I := 1 to 1000 do
  ListBox1.Items.Add(IntToStr(I));

rules.name: Comparison with True or False
rules.description: Comparing a Boolean with True or False is redundant; use the expression or not directly.
rules.bad:
if Visible = True then
  Show;
rules.good:
if Visible then
  Show;

rules.name: Assigned check before Free
rules.description: Free already checks for nil, so testing Assigned before Free or FreeAndNil is redundant.
rules.bad:
if Assigned(List) then
  List.Free;
rules.good: List.Free;

rules.name: raise in a finally block
rules.description: An exception raised in a finally block replaces the exception that is currently propagating, which is then lost.

rules.name: Redundant parentheses
rules.description: Parentheses around a whole condition or a single identifier add nothing. Off by default.
rules.bad:
if (Done) then
  Exit;
rules.good:
if Done then
  Exit;

rules.name: begin … end around a single statement
rules.description: A begin … end block that holds exactly one statement can be removed. Off by default.
rules.good:
if Done then
  Exit;

rules.name: with statement
rules.description: Inside a with block it is unclear which object an identifier belongs to, and a new member of the with object silently changes the meaning. Write the expression out or use a local variable.
rules.bad:
with Customer do
  Name := Edit.Text;
rules.good: Customer.Name := Edit.Text;

rules.name: Method too long
rules.description: The method has more code lines than the limit (default 60). Blank lines, comments, compiler directives and local routines do not count. Split the method into smaller ones. Set the limit with the option max, e.g. "rules": {"metric-method-length": {"max": 80}}.

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed number of statement lines.

rules.name: Nesting too deep
rules.description: The method nests if, case, loops and try deeper than the limit (default 4). else if stays on the level of its if. Leave early with Exit or Continue, or move inner parts into their own methods. Set the limit with the option max.

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed nesting depth.

rules.name: Cyclomatic complexity too high
rules.description: The cyclomatic complexity of the method is above the limit (default 15). It starts at 1 and adds 1 for every if, while, repeat and for, every case branch without else, every and/or in a condition and every except on; an except without on counts once. Many paths need many tests. Set the limit with the option max.
rules.good: Handlers[Kind]();

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed cyclomatic complexity.

rules.name: Cognitive complexity too high
rules.description: The cognitive complexity of the method is above the limit (default 15). Following SonarSource, if, case, loops and except handlers count 1 plus their nesting level; else, else if, goto and every sequence of equal logical operators count 1. Nested code is harder to read than code in sequence. Set the limit with the option max.
rules.bad:
if A then
  for I := 0 to N do
    if B and C or D then
      while E do
        F;

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed cognitive complexity.

rules.name: Too many parameters
rules.description: The method has more parameters than the limit (default 6). Group related values in a record or class. Set the limit with the option max.
rules.bad: procedure Book(const AName, AStreet, ACity, AZip: string; AAmount: Currency; ADate: TDate; ANote: string);
rules.good: procedure Book(const AAddress: TAddress; const AOrder: TOrder);

options.name: max
options.description: Highest allowed number of parameters.

rules.name: Open TODO comment
rules.description: A comment starts with a marker for open work: // TODO, // FIXME or the IDE to-do format { TODO 1 -oOwner -cCategory : Text }. The hint shows marker, priority, category, owner and text, so open work appears in the problem list. Off by default; switch it on in atlas.json, e.g. "rules": {"todo-comment": {"severity": "hint"}}. Completed entries ({ DONE … }) are never reported. The option keywords sets the markers (default ["TODO", "FIXME"]); it also applies to get_todos and --todos.
rules.bad:
// TODO 1 -oMarco -cGUI : set focus
Edit.Text := '';
rules.good:
Edit.Text := '';
Edit.SetFocus;

options.name: keywords
options.description: Markers of open TODO entries (letters only).

rules.name: Registered component without palette icon
rules.description: Every class passed to RegisterComponents needs a bitmap named after the class in upper case in a .dcr or .res included with {$R}. From Delphi 11 the sizes 16, 24 and 32 px (NAME16, NAME24, NAME32) are expected as well. Silent when the unit includes no readable resource file.
rules.bad:
{$R *.dcr} // without TMYBUTTON
RegisterComponents('Samples', [TMyButton]);
rules.good:
{$R *.dcr} // with TMYBUTTON16, TMYBUTTON24, TMYBUTTON32
RegisterComponents('Samples', [TMyButton]);

rules.name: Unresolved identifier
rules.description: An identifier in a statement is declared neither in the unit nor in the units it uses (like compiler error E2003). Checked while typing, without the compiler; with blocks, asm and anonymous methods are skipped.

rules.name: Deprecated symbol
rules.description: A routine, type, constant or member marked deprecated, platform or experimental is used (like compiler warnings W1000, W1002 and W1003). The editor strikes the name through; the message carries the reason from deprecated 'reason'. The declaration and the head of its implementation are not reported.

rules.name: Implicit package import
rules.description: In a package (.dpk) a unit from contains uses a unit that is neither in contains nor provided by a package in requires. The compiler pulls it in implicitly (W1033), which later causes duplicate units when another package also contains it. The quick fix adds the unit to contains.

rules.name: Type used before its declaration
rules.description: A class, interface, record or other type is used in a type declaration (field, parameter, result, property, generic argument, class of) but declared only further down in the same scope (like compiler error E2003). Ancestors, aliases and pointer types are not reported. Quick fixes: add a forward declaration at the start of the type block, merge type blocks (const, var and label sections in between move in front of the first block) or move a record up in front of its first user; without a safe fix the message gives the reason.

rules.name: Unneeded forward declaration
rules.description: A forward declaration whose type is not used before its full declaration in the same type block. Quick fix: remove it.

rules.name: Field created but never freed
rules.description: An object field that the constructor (or a private method it calls) creates with TClass.Create is never freed in the class (no Free, FreeAndNil, Destroy or DisposeOf): a memory leak. Components created with an owner other than nil, interface and record fields and the classes from the option ignoreTypes are exempt; TObjectList and TObjectDictionary fields are normal fields. Medium confidence. Quick fixes: free the field in the destructor, or free all owned objects of the class; a missing destructor is created with override and inherited. The objects are freed before inherited in reverse creation order, as Free or FreeAndNil (refactoring.freeFieldsStyle). Up to #918 the rule was called owned-field-not-freed; settings and suppressions with that id still apply.

options.name: ignoreTypes
options.description: Classes that are freed elsewhere; generic types match without type parameters.

rules.name: Unclear whether a created field must be freed
rules.description: An object field created in the constructor and not freed is also returned (Result := FField, Exit(FField)), handed to a property of another object or to its Add…, Insert…, Register…, Attach…, Push or Enqueue, assigned without Create or writable through a property (write FField). Whether the class still owns the object is up to the developer, so there is no quick fix.

rules.name: Precedence of not overlooked
rules.description: In Pascal not binds more tightly than in and comparisons: not X in Set means (not X) in Set, not A = B means (not A) = B, and on integers not works bitwise. The rule reports these forms when the declared type of the operand shows that this cannot be meant (not Boolean). Quick fix: add parentheses, not (X in Set).
rules.bad:
if not Zustand in [zsOffen, zsGesperrt] then
  Bearbeiten;
rules.good:
if not (Zustand in [zsOffen, zsGesperrt]) then
  Bearbeiten;

rules.name: Empty statement after then, do or else
rules.description: A semicolon right after then, do or else ends the statement: the following line always runs, or the loop spins empty. An empty begin … end after then, do or else is reported too, unless it contains an explanatory comment (option allowCommented). A semicolon right before end, until, except or finally changes nothing and is not reported. Quick fix: remove the semicolon.
rules.bad:
if Liste.Count = 0 then;
  raise EKeineDaten.Create('Keine Daten');
rules.good:
if Liste.Count = 0 then
  raise EKeineDaten.Create('Keine Daten');

options.name: allowCommented
options.description: Do not report begin { intentionally empty } end.

rules.name: Loop runs one step too far
rules.description: for I := 0 to List.Count or to Length(A) over zero-based lists and arrays reads one element past the end when the body indexes List[I] or A[I]. With one-based strings it is the other way round: S[0] and for I := 0 to Length(S) read before the first character; {$ZEROBASEDSTRINGS ON} is taken into account. Quick fix: add - 1 or use High(A); for strings Low(S) and High(S). The option countNames lists the names that return a count.
rules.bad:
for I := 0 to Kunden.Count do
  Ausgabe(Kunden[I].Name);
rules.good:
for I := 0 to Kunden.Count - 1 do
  Ausgabe(Kunden[I].Name);

options.name: countNames
options.description: Names that return a count (property like Count or function like Length).

rules.name: List modified inside its own loop
rules.description: Delete, Remove, Add or another method from the option mutatingMethods is called on the list that the loop is walking forwards by index or with for … in. Forwards, Delete skips the next element and runs past the end, Add is not visited and Insert visits the same element twice; with for … in the RTL raises an exception. A Break or Exit directly after the call ends the loop and stays silent, downto loops too. Quick fix for index loops: rewrite as downto; for for … in collect the elements and change the list after the loop.

options.name: mutatingMethods
options.description: Methods that change the list.

rules.name: Object used after Free
rules.description: After X.Free, X.Destroy, X.DisposeOf, FreeAndNil(X) or Dispose(X), X is used again without a new assignment: a method, field, index or X^, with X, and after Free also Assigned(X) (always True) or a second Free. The rule follows the data flow of the routine; an assignment to X, passing X to a routine, @X and after FreeAndNil a check for nil end the path, ways only through a possible exception are left out. Confidence high when release and access stand one after the other in the same block, otherwise medium. No automatic fix; the action jumps to the release.
rules.bad:
Bericht.Free;
Protokoll.Add('Seiten: ' + IntToStr(Bericht.Seiten));
rules.good:
Protokoll.Add('Seiten: ' + IntToStr(Bericht.Seiten));
Bericht.Free;

rules.name: Used first, checked for nil later
rules.description: X is dereferenced (X.Field, X.Method, X^) and only afterwards checked with Assigned(X), X <> nil or X = nil. Either the check is superfluous or the access before it can crash. Reported only when every path to the check passes the access and X was not checked before; a new assignment, passing X to a routine and, for fields and global variables, any call in between end the path. Medium confidence. When the check is an if without else directly after the access in the same block, the quick fix moves the access into it.

rules.name: Field freed, reference stays
rules.description: FField.Free in a method outside the destructor, and a path to the end of the method does not set the field again. A later access or a second Free hits freed memory. Setting it again means an assignment or the call of a method of the same class that assigns the field. Fields are those of the class declaration in the unit. Destructors, methods with [TearDown] or [TearDownFixture], methods only called from these and the methods from the option ignoreMethods are exempt. Medium confidence. Quick fix: FreeAndNil(FField).

options.name: ignoreMethods
options.description: Methods in which Free without nil is allowed.

rules.name: Constructor or destructor without inherited
rules.description: A constructor, or an override of Destroy, AfterConstruction or BeforeDestruction, does not call inherited, in any class whose ancestor is not TObject. Constructors are reported only if an ancestor declares a constructor of its own (file, index or a known RTL/VCL class) and the constructor does not call another constructor of the same class. For components, Destroy is reported only by component-missing-inherited. High confidence. Quick fix: insert inherited; at the end of Destroy and BeforeDestruction, at the start of constructors and AfterConstruction; a constructor with parameters without override gets inherited Create;.

options.name: methods
options.description: Checked methods; Create stands for all constructors whose name starts with Create.

rules.name: Destroy called instead of Free
rules.description: Obj.Destroy is called directly as a statement. If Obj is nil, the call crashes; Free checks for nil first and is the usual way to release an object. inherited Destroy and calls of a destructor with arguments are exempt. High confidence. Quick fix: Destroy becomes Free.
rules.bad: Verbindung.Destroy;
rules.good: Verbindung.Free;

rules.name: FillChar, Move or GetMem on managed types
rules.description: FillChar, ZeroMemory, FillMemory, Move, CopyMemory, GetMem or FreeMem on a variable whose type contains strings, interfaces, dynamic arrays or variants (records, static arrays and aliases are resolved in the file and in the index). Reference counts are overwritten or skipped: leaks, double frees, access violations. Only plain variables (X, @X, P^) are checked; array elements such as S[1] and types that cannot be resolved stay silent. High confidence. Quick fixes: FillChar(X, SizeOf(X), 0) becomes X := Default(T), Move(A, B, SizeOf(T)) becomes B := A, GetMem(P, SizeOf(T)) becomes New(P) and FreeMem(P) becomes Dispose(P); otherwise Initialize and Finalize help.
rules.bad: FillChar(Adresse, SizeOf(Adresse), 0);
rules.good: Adresse := Default(TAdresse);

rules.name: threadvar with a managed type
rules.description: Delphi does not finalize threadvar variables. A string, interface, dynamic array or variant in a threadvar (also inside a record or static array) leaks in every thread that ends. Types are resolved in the file and in the index. High confidence. No quick fix: release the value at the end of the thread (for example set it to '' or nil in TThread.Execute), or store a pointer or a fixed-size buffer instead.
rules.bad:
threadvar
  LetzteMeldung: string;
rules.good:
threadvar
  LetzteMeldung: PChar;

rules.name: PChar of a temporary string
rules.description: PChar (PWideChar, PAnsiChar) of a temporary string, such as a concatenation with a string (S + '.bak') or a function result (IntToStr(N)), is stored in a variable, a field or Result, or passed to PostMessage, PostThreadMessage, SendNotifyMessage or SendMessageCallback (also behind LPARAM(…)). The temporary string is released after the statement, so the pointer points to freed memory. Passing it to an ordinary call such as CopyFile is fine. High confidence. Quick fix for local variables: keep the intermediate result in an inline string variable.
rules.bad:
Ziel := PChar(Pfad + '.bak');
CopyFile(PChar(Pfad), Ziel, False);

rules.name: out parameter read before it is set
rules.description: An out parameter is read before the routine sets it on some path through the control flow. For managed types (string, interfaces, dynamic arrays, Variant) the caller has already cleared it, so the old value is gone; for other types the value is undefined. Usually var was meant. Uses the control flow graph cannot follow (passing the parameter to a routine, setting a field of it, @Param) stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: out becomes var in the implementation and in the declaration.

rules.name: Find or Duplicates on an unsorted TStringList
rules.description: Find on a TStringList or THashedStringList that is created in the unit but never sorted: Find searches binary and returns wrong results on an unsorted list. The same holds for Duplicates := dupIgnore or dupError, which only works on sorted lists. Sorted counts as Sorted := True (or any value other than False), Sort, CustomSort, Create(Duplicates, True, ...) and with List do. A list passed to a routine or assigned to another variable stays silent. Locals are tracked per routine, fields across the unit. Medium confidence. Quick fixes: Sorted := True after the creation (not offered when the list uses Insert, Move or Exchange, which raise on sorted lists) and, for if List.Find(S, I) then, I := List.IndexOf(S) with if I >= 0.

rules.name: Writeln in a program without console
rules.description: Write, Writeln, Read or Readln on standard input or output in a program without a console: at run time Writeln raises EInOutError (I/O error 105), Readln I/O error 104. The application type comes from DCC_ConsoleTarget in the .dproj and {$APPTYPE CONSOLE} in the .dpr (also inside {$IFDEF}); units are only checked when they belong to the loaded project, a .dpr without project on its own. Libraries and packages stay silent. Calls with a text file as first argument, calls under if IsConsole, routines of the same name declared in the unit and Read/Write inside methods (TStream.Read) are exempt. High confidence. Quick fix for Write and Writeln: replace with OutputDebugString(PChar(...)) and add Winapi.Windows; numbers and Boolean go through IntToStr, FloatToStr and BoolToStr. Option replacement sets another target, e.g. Log.Info or Logger.Log(TLogLevel.Info, %s). No fix for width specifiers (X:5) or arguments of unknown type.

options.name: replacement
options.description: Replacement for Write and Writeln in the quick fix; %s stands for the text.

rules.name: raise in a destructor
rules.description: raise in a destructor (also class destructor) that no except inside the destructor catches. The exception aborts the destruction: inherited Destroy no longer runs, the object stays half freed, and in a finally of the caller it hides the original exception. A raise in the try part of a try..except is caught; raise in the except or finally part, including a bare raise; to re-raise, is reported. Nested routines and anonymous methods are exempt. Calls that raise are not followed. High confidence. No quick fix: log the state or release it without an exception.

rules.name: Duplicate condition or identical branches
rules.description: The same condition twice in an if ... else if chain (the later branch is never reached), identical then and else branches, the same operand twice in an and, or or xor chain, and comparisons of an expression with itself (X = X, X < X). Usually a copy error. Expressions are compared by their tokens without whitespace, comments and case. Chains with calls that may change state (anything but SameText, Length, Assigned, Pos and similar pure functions, or Read, Next, Pop, Random ...) stay silent, as do float self-comparisons (NaN check X <> X) and comparisons on class members such as TFoo.Shared = TFoo.Shared. High confidence. No quick fix; the action jumps to the first occurrence.
rules.bad:
if Betrag > 1000 then
  Stufe := 3
else if Betrag > 500 then
  Stufe := 2
else if Betrag > 1000 then
  Stufe := 1;
rules.good:
if Betrag > 1000 then
  Stufe := 3
else if Betrag > 500 then
  Stufe := 2
else if Betrag > 100 then
  Stufe := 1;

rules.name: case over an enumeration without all values
rules.description: A case over an enumerated type without else does not cover all values; a value added later silently falls through. The message names the missing values. The type of the selector (variable, parameter, field or chain A.B) comes from name resolution, the values from the index or the unit itself; aliases are followed. Ranges (bsNeu..bsBezahlt) and lists count as present. Selectors with calls, integer and unknown types stay silent. With option requireElse a case with else is reported as well. High confidence. Quick fix "Fehlende Werte ergänzen (n)" adds empty branches in declaration order before else or end, with type prefix when the labels use one ({$SCOPEDENUMS ON}).

options.name: requireElse
options.description: Also report case statements with else when values are missing.

rules.name: Paired calls without try/finally
rules.description: Generalises lock-without-finally (whose lock pairs stay there) to other pairs: DisableControls/EnableControls, BeginUpdate/EndUpdate, FindFirst/FindClose (also in if FindFirst(...) = 0 then begin ... end), Reset, Rewrite or Append/CloseFile, GetMem or AllocMem/FreeMem and Screen.Cursor := ... with a later Screen.Cursor := .... Reported when the closing call stands unprotected later in the same statement list with at least one statement in between; an exception there leaves the state hanging. Both calls must use the same receiver or argument. Overlapping pairs are reported together. High confidence. Quick fix: wrap the statements in between in try/finally with the closing calls, when the closing calls follow each other directly. Option pairs adds own pairs.

options.name: pairs
options.description: Additional pairs as [{"open": "Freeze", "close": "Thaw"}], optionally with openArg/closeArg.

rules.name: Application.ProcessMessages in loops
rules.description: Application.ProcessMessages inside a for, while or repeat loop, or directly in an event handler (a method with a Sender parameter), opens the door for re-entrancy: the user clicks again, closes the form or starts the operation twice. Calls inside anonymous methods are left to thread-vcl-access; other objects' ProcessMessages methods are ignored. Medium confidence, no quick fix: move the work to a thread or TTask, or disable the trigger until it is done. Option allowIn lists methods where it is allowed.

options.name: allowIn
options.description: Methods in which ProcessMessages is allowed, as Name or Class.Name.

rules.name: Unchecked conversion of user input
rules.description: StrToInt, StrToInt64, StrToFloat, StrToDate, StrToDateTime or StrToCurr applied directly to user input (Edit.Text, Grid.Cells[...], Memo.Lines[...], also inside Trim) outside the try part of a try/except. Invalid input raises EConvertError with an English message. try/finally does not count as protection. Medium confidence. Quick fix for X := StrToInt(Edit.Text); as its own statement, when X is a variable or field of the matching type: if not TryStrToInt(Edit.Text, X) then raise EConvertError.Create('X ist keine Zahl'). format-without-settings additionally reports locale-dependent conversions without TFormatSettings. Options functions and sources choose the checked conversions and the properties that count as input.
rules.bad: Menge := StrToInt(edtMenge.Text);
rules.good:
if not TryStrToInt(edtMenge.Text, Menge) then
  raise EConvertError.Create('Menge ist keine Zahl');

options.name: functions
options.description: Checked conversions.

options.name: sources
options.description: Properties that count as user input.

rules.name: Dictionary access without key check
rules.description: Dict[Key] or Dict.Items[Key] is read on a TDictionary or TObjectDictionary (also through a type alias of the file) although neither ContainsKey nor TryGetValue checked the same key earlier in the routine. The rule stays silent when the routine fills the dictionary itself beforehand (Add, AddOrSetValue, TryAdd, Dict[K] := ...) or when the key stems from Keys or the pairs (for K in Dict.Keys, Names := Dict.Keys.ToArray, for Pair in Dict with K := Pair.Key). A missing key raises EListError. Medium confidence. Quick fix for X := Dict[Key]; as its own statement, when X is a variable of the value type: if not Dict.TryGetValue(Key, X) then X := 0 (or '', False, Default(T)).
rules.bad: Preis := Preise[Artikel.Nummer];
rules.good:
if not Preise.TryGetValue(Artikel.Nummer, Preis) then
  Preis := 0;

rules.name: Local name shadows field or property
rules.description: A parameter, local or inline variable has the same name as a field or property of the class (also inherited and visible there, resolved through the file and the symbol index) or as a global variable of the unit declared before the routine. Especially treacherous in form methods: Caption, Name, Tag, Left. If VCL is not in the index, the members of TComponent and TControl are known when the ancestor chain ends at a VCL base class. Parameters of event handlers (with Sender) are skipped because the event type dictates the signature. High confidence. Quick fix: rename to AName (parameter, also in the declaration) or LName (local variable) within the routine. Option ignore lists name patterns that are never reported (default Sender, Value).

options.name: ignore
options.description: Name patterns (* and ?) that are never reported.

rules.name: if that only assigns True or False
rules.description: if B then X := True else X := False (also with begin/end and the values swapped), if B then Exit(True) else Exit(False) and if B then Exit(True); followed by Exit(False); can be written directly. Complements bool-compare. High confidence. Quick fix: X := B, X := not B or Exit(B); negations are simplified (not B becomes B), compound conditions are wrapped in parentheses. Without a fix when comments stand inside the if.
rules.bad:
if Betrag > 0 then
  Result := True
else
  Result := False;
rules.good: Result := Betrag > 0;

rules.name: Comparison through UpperCase or LowerCase
rules.description: UpperCase(A) = UpperCase(B), LowerCase(A) <> 'x', AnsiUpperCase(...) or A.ToUpper = B.ToUpper creates two strings for one comparison. SameText (AnsiSameText for the Ansi functions and the Unicode string helpers) is shorter and faster. A literal is only accepted if the conversion does not change it; UpperCase(A) = LowerCase(B) and UpperCase(A) = 'ja' are left alone because they are different mistakes. Does not replace the string helper modernisation of #71. High confidence. Quick fix: SameText(A, B) or not SameText(A, B).
rules.bad: if UpperCase(Land) = UpperCase(Standard) then
rules.good: if SameText(Land, Standard) then

rules.name: Number without a name in code
rules.description: Number literals (decimal, $hex, floating point, with sign) in statements, outside const sections, types, array bounds and subranges. Allowed values are configurable; DFM coordinates and tests can be excluded through exclude. Off by default and low confidence: it shows up once the rule is switched on and minConfidence is low. Quick fix: Introduce constant (#50) in the const section of the routine.
rules.bad:
if Tage > 42 then
  Mahnen;

options.name: allowed
options.description: Numbers that are never reported.

rules.name: Line too long
rules.description: Lines longer than the limit max (default 120 characters, matching the rulers from #710). Tabs count up to the next tab stop of format.indentSize. Lines that are only too long because of a string or, with ignoreComments, a comment are not reported. Lines over 1023 characters are always reported as an error regardless of max, because the compiler stops there (F2069). Off by default. Quick fix: Wrap line after commas or before binary operators, where the pieces then fit.
rules.bad: Ergebnis := Rechner.Berechne(Kunde.Rabattstufe, Bestellung.Positionen, Lager.Verfuegbarkeit(Artikel), Steuer.Satz(Land));
rules.good:
Ergebnis := Rechner.Berechne(Kunde.Rabattstufe, Bestellung.Positionen, Lager.Verfuegbarkeit(Artikel),
  Steuer.Satz(Land));

options.name: max
options.description: Maximum line length in characters.

options.name: ignoreStrings
options.description: Do not report lines that are only too long because of a string.

options.name: ignoreComments
options.description: Do not report lines that are only too long because of a comment.

rules.name: Class with too many members
rules.description: The class has more members than the limit (default 40): field names, methods, properties with their own type and class var. Properties that only raise visibility (property Align;) and nested types do not count; a nested class is measured on its own. Also shown in the metrics lens above the class. Split the class or move parts into helper classes; Move class to own unit (#103) helps when the unit is crowded too.

options.name: max
options.description: Maximum number of members per class.

rules.name: Unit too long
rules.description: The unit has more lines than the limit (default 2000), counted up to the final end. Only units are measured, not programs or packages. Also shown in the metrics lens above the unit name. Move classes into their own units with Move class to own unit (#103).
rules.bad: unit Kasse.Haupt;  { 2140 lines }
rules.good: unit Kasse.Haupt;  { 900 lines; TBeleg in Kasse.Beleg }

options.name: max
options.description: Maximum number of lines per unit.

rules.name: Too many units in uses
rules.description: The unit uses more units than the limit (default 30), interface and implementation together. The finding sits on the first uses. Programs and libraries are not checked, because their uses lists the units of the project. Also shown in the metrics lens above uses. Many dependencies usually mean the unit does too much; Move class to own unit (#103) splits it.
rules.bad:
uses
  { 34 units in interface and implementation }
rules.good:
uses
  { 12 units; reports in Kasse.Berichte }

options.name: max
options.description: Maximum number of units in all uses clauses.

rules.name: Public field
rules.description: Fields in the public or published section of a class. The section without a visibility keyword only counts for classes without an ancestor or with TObject, because the form designer puts its fields there. Records are excluded unless includeRecords is set; class var is not reported. Off by default. Quick fix: Encapsulate field moves the field as FName into a private section at the end of the class and adds property Name read FName write FName in the old section; accesses from outside stay valid.

options.name: includeRecords
options.description: Also report fields of records.

rules.name: Global variable in interface
rules.description: var or threadvar in the interface section of a unit: every unit that uses it can read and change the value. The form variable created by the designer (frmMain: TfrmMain, for classes derived from TForm, TFrame, TDataModule or any class in a unit with a form file) is excluded unless includeFormVariables is set. Off by default. Move the variable into the implementation section and offer a function or property instead.

options.name: includeFormVariables
options.description: Also report the form variables created by the designer.

rules.name: Commented-out code
rules.description: At least minLines consecutive comment lines (// per line or a multi-line { } comment) that parse as statements, declarations or class members. Prose at the start and end of the block is ignored, and at least half the lines must look like code (;, :=, begin, end, then, do). XMLDoc (///) and comments before the first token (license headers) are never reported. Confidence medium. Version control keeps the old code; the fix removes the lines.
rules.good: Speichern;

options.name: minLines
options.description: Minimum number of consecutive commented-out code lines.

rules.name: TThread.Queue(nil, …) in a package
rules.description: TThread.Queue(nil, …) or TThread.ForceQueue(nil, …) in a unit of a design-time or runtime package: the entry belongs to no thread, so nobody removes it when the package is unloaded, and CheckSynchronize may call it afterwards in memory that no longer holds the code. Package units are recognized through the .dpk or .dproj of the loaded project (a .dpk on its own without project). A line with the comment from okMarker (default mainthread-ok) is exempt. High confidence. Quick fix: rewrite to the wrapper from the wrapper option (default TAtlasMainThread.Queue, ForceQueue for ForceQueue); with a parenthesis the wrapper text is put in front of the remaining arguments. ForceQueue with a delay gets no quick fix. The command-line linter reads the .dpk files below the checked folder. Does the same as Tools/Check-MainThreadQueue.ps1 for any plugin project; the script stays for checks without the Atlas server.

options.name: wrapper
options.description: Replacement for TThread.Queue(nil, in the quick fix.

options.name: okMarker
options.description: Comment that exempts a line.

rules.name: IDE notifier without RemoveNotifier
rules.description: AddNotifier on IOTAServices, IOTAEditorServices, IOTAModule and so on (or another pair from registerPairs) whose index never reaches RemoveNotifier: the call is a statement without assignment, or the variable it is assigned to is never passed to RemoveNotifier in the unit (in finalization, a destructor or Destroyed). The IDE then calls the notifier after the package is unloaded, in memory that no longer holds the code. Register… calls inside the procedure Register are exempt: the IDE removes those wizards itself. Medium confidence. Quick fix in methods: keep the index in a field (FNotifierIndex in the private section) and add RemoveNotifier to the destructor, which is created if missing; in procedures of the unit: a global variable initialized with -1 and RemoveNotifier in finalization. No quick fix when the receiver is a parameter or local variable.

options.name: registerPairs
options.description: Pairs of the Open Tools API as [{"open": "AddNotifier", "close": "RemoveNotifier"}]; replaces the default.

rules.name: DUnitX test without assert
rules.description: A [Test] or [TestCase] method that calls no check, neither itself nor through methods of the same class or routines of the unit: it is always green. Calls matching assertPatterns (default Assert.*, WillRaise*, Check*), System.Assert and calls on classes with Assert in their name (TRuleAssert.Reports) count as checks. Tests with [WillRaise] or [Ignore] stay silent. High confidence. Quick fixes: insert Assert.Pass as a placeholder, or jump to the method.

options.name: assertPatterns
options.description: Calls that count as a check, as patterns with * and ?; replaces the default.

rules.name: Event called without Assigned check
rules.description: FOnChange(Self) or OnChange(Self) is called in a method of the class without Assigned(FOnChange) or FOnChange <> nil guarding the call: without a handler an access violation follows. Events are fields and properties of the class with a method pointer or reference type (procedure ... of object, reference to ..., TNotifyEvent, TProc/TFunc, types ending in Event, procedural types of the unit or the index). Guards: the then branch of a condition with Assigned (also while), the else branch of not Assigned, "Assigned(F) and" before the call, or "if not Assigned(F) then Exit/raise" before it, including a flag variable or a parameterless method of the class whose Result contains Assigned(F). Fields that a constructor sets to a value (injected dependencies such as FReadText := AReadText), properties reading them and local names that shadow the event stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: wrap the call in "if Assigned(F) then" when it is a statement of its own in a block.

rules.name: Item of an owning list freed as well
rules.description: An item of a TObjectList/TObjectList<T> (OwnsObjects, default True) or of a TObjectDictionary with doOwnsValues is freed with Free, FreeAndNil, Destroy or DisposeOf, directly (List[I].Free, List.Items[I].Free) or through a variable taken from List[I], List.First/Last or a for-in loop over the list or Dictionary.Values. The list frees the item itself on Delete, Remove, Clear, an assignment to List[I], or at the latest when it is freed: a double free. A list is owning when the unit creates it that way (TObjectList without False, TObjectDictionary with doOwnsValues) or declares it as TObjectList without creating it, and no OwnsObjects := False follows. Extract in the same routine keeps the rule silent. High confidence. Quick fixes: remove the Free (the whole loop when it only frees), Delete or Remove instead of Free, Extract instead of Remove.

rules.name: Object created and lost at once
rules.description: TStringList.Create; as a statement of its own: the object is created but stored nowhere and never freed (memory leak). Silent for components with an owner (first argument Self, Owner, AOwner, Application, or a TComponent descendant with an argument other than nil), threads (they free themselves with FreeOnTerminate), records, unknown classes with arguments and classes listed in selfRegistering. High confidence. Quick fix: assign to a new local variable and wrap the following statements of the block in try/finally with Free.

options.name: selfRegistering
options.description: Classes that register themselves in their constructor, as patterns with * and ?; Create as a statement stays silent for them.

rules.name: Message handler without inherited
rules.description: A method with message WM_... or CM_... calls neither inherited nor DefaultHandler (or DefWindowProc, CallWindowProc). The default handling of the VCL or Windows is lost: no realignment on WM_SIZE, no closing on WM_CLOSE, no painting on WM_PAINT. The message names the consequence for common messages. Silent for classes without an ancestor, for messages listed in swallow (default WM_ERASEBKGND) and for handlers that set Msg.Result themselves (deliberate answer such as MA_NOACTIVATE). Medium confidence. Quick fix: insert inherited; at the start.

options.name: swallow
options.description: Messages that may be handled without inherited; replaces the default.

rules.name: String index from 0 or Pos result compared with -1
rules.description: The classic string routines count from 1: Copy(S, 0, N) and Insert(T, S, 0) only work like 1 by chance, Delete(S, 0, N) deletes nothing. The string must be known: declared type in the file, literal, or .Text/.Caption; dynamic arrays (0-based) stay silent. Pos, PosEx and AnsiPos return 0 for no match: Pos(...) > -1, >= 0 and <> -1 are always true, = -1 and < 0 never. Conversely S.IndexOf(...) > 0 or >= 1 misses a match at the start, < 1 or <= 0 counts it as not found (medium confidence; LastIndexOf stays silent, where > 0 usually means "not at the start"). High confidence for Delete and Pos. Quick fix: start value 1 or the corrected comparison (> 0, = 0, >= 0, < 0).
rules.bad:
if Pos(';', Zeile) > -1 then
  Felder := Copy(Zeile, 0, Pos(';', Zeile) - 1);
rules.good:
if Pos(';', Zeile) > 0 then
  Felder := Copy(Zeile, 1, Pos(';', Zeile) - 1);

rules.name: DelimitedText without StrictDelimiter
rules.description: List.DelimitedText := ... after List.Delimiter := ... in the same routine without StrictDelimiter being set: DelimitedText then also splits at spaces, 'Max Muster;Berlin' becomes three entries instead of two. For fields, StrictDelimiter anywhere in the unit counts (often in the constructor); StrictDelimiter := False is deliberate and stays silent, as does DelimitedText without a Delimiter of its own. High confidence. Quick fix: insert StrictDelimiter := True; before the assignment.
rules.bad:
Teile.Delimiter := ';';
Teile.DelimitedText := Zeile;

rules.name: Self passed as interface during construction
rules.description: Self is passed as an interface while reference counting can already free the object. Only two real error cases are reported: (1) a class with its own reference counting (an _Release in the class chain frees the object, no class overrides NewInstance, the chain is known up to TObject) passes Self as an interface in a constructor or in AfterConstruction: the counter goes from 0 to 1 and back to 0, the object is destroyed before construction ends. (2) A TInterfacedObject descendant passes Self as an interface in AfterConstruction after inherited: inherited AfterConstruction has already removed the protective count from NewInstance. In the constructor of a TInterfacedObject descendant Self is protected and the rule stays silent. Passing counts as Self as IX, IX(Self), an argument whose parameter is an interface in all known overloads, and an assignment to an interface variable. High confidence. Quick fix in case 2: move the statement before inherited.

rules.name: Comparison with Null instead of VarIsNull or IsNull
rules.description: X = Null or X <> Null compares a variant with Null. The result depends on the global System.Variants.NullEqualityRule: with the default ncrLoose the comparison works as expected, with ncrStrict it is never true and with ncrError it raises an exception. A library, a test framework or another part of the project can change the rule. VarIsNull(X) and Field.IsNull check independently of it. Reported only where the comparison stands on its own (condition, argument, assignment); not X = Null binds as (not X) = Null and gets no quick fix. High confidence. Quick fix: Field.IsNull for X.Value on FieldByName, FindField, Fields[...], ParamByName, Params[...] or a field of type T...Field/T...Param, otherwise VarIsNull(X); with <> preceded by not.
rules.bad:
if qryKunde.FieldByName('Geburtstag').Value = Null then
  Alter := 0;
rules.good:
if qryKunde.FieldByName('Geburtstag').IsNull then
  Alter := 0;

rules.name: Number cast to enumeration without check
rules.description: TStatus(N) with an enumeration type declared in the file or the index, where N comes from a call listed in the option sources (FieldByName, ReadInteger, AsInteger, StrToInt): directly in the argument or via a variable that is not read (checked) between its assignment and the cast. A value outside the range yields an invalid enumeration value that falls through case statements. EnsureRange, Min or Max in the argument count as a check; constants, arithmetic and unknown types stay silent. For enumerations with explicit ordinal values the range is given as Ord(Low(T))..Ord(High(T)). Medium confidence. Quick fix for a direct source in a statement of its own: helper variable, InRange check with raise EConvertError before it, System.Math added to uses.
rules.bad: Status := TStatus(qry.FieldByName('Status').AsInteger);

options.name: sources
options.description: Calls whose result counts as unchecked.

rules.name: CreateProcess with a read-only command line
rules.description: CreateProcess (CreateProcessW) and CreateProcessAsUser write into the buffer of lpCommandLine. A PChar on memory that cannot be written causes an access violation. Reported for PChar(...)/PWideChar(...) on: a string literal or constant; a concatenation of exactly one literal and one value (if the value is empty, the RTL returns the literal itself); a local string variable whose last assignment before the call is one of these, without UniqueString afterwards; a string parameter (medium confidence, the caller may pass a literal). Function results such as Format and concatenations with several parts are writable heap strings and stay silent, as does CreateProcessA, which copies the command line itself. Quick fix: copy the command line into a local variable and call UniqueString; for a variable, UniqueString before the statement. No quick fix in loop conditions.
rules.bad: CreateProcess(nil, PChar('notepad.exe ' + Datei), nil, nil, False, 0, nil, nil, SI, PI);

rules.name: Access to a form that is not created yet
rules.description: The constructor, AfterConstruction or the OnCreate handler of an automatically created form or data module uses the global variable of another form that the .dpr creates later with Application.CreateForm. The variable is still nil at that point. The order comes from the .dpr of the project the unit belongs to; the OnCreate handler from the form file (FormCreate or DataModuleCreate without one). Silent when the routine checks the variable (Assigned, comparison with nil), assigns it itself, creates it with CreateForm or declares a local name of the same name, and for forms that are not created automatically. Each variable is reported once per routine. Medium confidence. No quick fix: change the order in the .dpr or move the access to OnShow.

rules.name: General exception handler before a specific one
rules.description: In a try..except with several on handlers the first matching handler wins. A handler for a class that an earlier handler already catches is never reached: its code is dead and the special treatment never runs. Reported when an earlier handler names the same class, an ancestor of it, Exception (covers every exception class) or TObject. Ancestors come from the unit, the project index and a table of known RTL, VCL and FireDAC exception classes (for example EStreamError > EFOpenError, EIntError > ERangeError); unknown classes are only compared with Exception and TObject. Quick fix: move the specific handler before the general one (only when both handlers stand on their own lines). A duplicate handler for the same class is reported without a quick fix.

rules.name: raise E instead of raise in a handler
rules.description: raise E; in an on E: … handler raises the caught exception object again as a new raise. The RTL does not free the object twice, but the exception now starts at the handler: ExceptAddr and the call stack of tools such as madExcept or JclDebug point to the handler instead of the original fault, and the original location is lost. raise; re-raises the current exception unchanged. Also reported for raise E at …, then without a quick fix. Silent when the handler takes the object over with AcquireExceptionObject or assigns a new object to the variable, inside anonymous methods and for handlers without a variable name. High confidence. Quick fix: raise E; → raise;.

rules.name: Blocking call in the main thread
rules.description: Sleep, WaitFor, WaitForSingleObject, WaitForMultipleObjects or Wait in methods of forms and frames (classes that inherit from TForm, TCustomForm, TFrame or TCustomFrame) and in event handlers (methods with a Sender parameter) outside thread classes. The user interface freezes while the call waits; if the other thread waits for Synchronize, the program hangs. WaitFor without a timeout on a variable names the risk of the Synchronize deadlock. Sleep, WaitForSingleObject and WaitForMultipleObjects count only without a receiver (or with Winapi.Windows), WaitFor and Wait only on a receiver. A literal timeout below maxSleepMs (Sleep(10), WaitForSingleObject(H, 0)) stays silent, except a short Sleep in a waiting loop without Application.ProcessMessages. Anonymous methods are skipped (TTask.Run, TThread.Queue), nested routines belong to their method. Medium confidence. No quick fix: move the work into TTask.Run and report the result with TThread.Queue.

options.name: maxSleepMs
options.description: Literal timeouts below this value (milliseconds) are not reported; a short Sleep in a waiting loop still is.

options.name: calls
options.description: Calls that block. Other names are reported regardless of their arguments.

rules.name: Thread loop without Terminated
rules.description: A while or repeat loop in TThread.Execute, or in a method of the thread class that is only called from there (also through other such methods, including nested routines), does not check Terminated. Terminate then has no effect, and WaitFor or Free hang when the program shuts down. Reported for endless loops (while True, until False) and for waiting loops with Sleep, WaitFor, WaitForSingleObject, WaitForMultipleObjects, MsgWaitForMultipleObjects, Wait or Yield whose condition and body never mention Terminated or CheckTerminated. Thread classes come from the unit and the index. Bounded loops, for loops, anonymous methods and classes that override TerminatedSet (they end their loops another way) stay silent. High confidence. Quick fix: add Terminated to the loop condition (while True → while not Terminated, otherwise and not Terminated; until False → until Terminated, otherwise or Terminated).

rules.name: Anonymous thread never started
rules.description: TThread.CreateAnonymousThread(…) creates the thread suspended with FreeOnTerminate set. Without Start the thread never runs, and because it never terminates it is never freed either. Reported for the call as a statement of its own and for a local variable (also an inline variable) that is never started with Start or Resume and not passed on (argument, assignment, Result, field). Setting properties such as FreeOnTerminate or OnTerminate does not count as passing on. High confidence. Quick fix: append .Start; for a variable, T.Start; after the last statement of the same block that mentions it.

rules.name: Exception in TTask gets lost
rules.description: TTask.Run(…) or TTask.Create(…).Start whose result is never kept or queried with Wait, Status or similar, and whose anonymous method has no try … except. An exception in the task disappears silently. Also reported for a local variable that is never mentioned again (for TTask.Create only in V.Start). Silent for kept results (fields, Result, any other use of the variable) and for method references, whose body the rule cannot see. Medium confidence. Quick fix: wrap the body in try … except and report the message on the main thread through TThread.Queue with ShowMessage (adds Vcl.Dialogs, or FMX.Dialogs in FireMonkey units, and System.SysUtils to the uses clause when missing); only when begin and end of the anonymous method stand on their own lines.

rules.name: Dataset loop without Next
rules.description: while not Q.Eof do without Q.Next in the body, or with Next only on some of the paths that continue the loop (an if without else, Continue before Next). The loop spins forever on the same record. Delete, MoveBy, Last, Close, FindNext and Free also count as moving on; Break, Exit, Abort and raise end the loop. Nested while and for loops are not trusted to run. When Q is passed on in the body (argument, assignment, with), the called code may move the record pointer and the rule stays silent. High confidence when Next is missing entirely, medium when only some paths miss it. Quick fix: insert Q.Next; at the end of the begin … end body (only when Next is missing entirely).

rules.name: Edit or Append without Post
rules.description: After Edit, Append or Insert (without arguments) on a dataset, the same routine calls neither Post nor Cancel (nor CheckBrowseMode). The change stays open and is silently lost on scrolling or saved unexpectedly later; on an exception in between, nothing cancels it. Silent when another routine of the unit posts or cancels the same dataset (an Edit button with a separate Save button) and when the dataset is passed on after Edit (argument, assignment, with). Medium confidence. Quick fix: wrap the following statements that use the dataset in try … except, with Post at the end of the try part and Cancel; raise; in the except part.

rules.name: Transaction without Rollback
rules.description: StartTransaction without Rollback in the except part of the try that directly follows. On an exception the transaction stays open and holds locks. Recognized for FireDAC (TFDConnection, TFDTransaction), IBX and dbExpress (StartTransaction/Commit/Rollback), dbExpress from XE (BeginTransaction/CommitFreeAndNil/RollbackFreeAndNil, also as T := Conn.BeginTransaction) and ADO (BeginTrans/CommitTrans/RollbackTrans). The option pairs replaces these pairs with your own. The Rollback may sit in a try … except inside a try … finally that follows directly. Silent when another routine of the unit rolls back the same connection (transaction across several events). High confidence. Quick fix: wrap the statements up to the Commit of the same block in try … except with Rollback (with the arguments of the Commit) and raise; only when a Commit follows in the same block.

options.name: pairs
options.description: Transaction methods per library as [{"start": …, "commit": …, "rollback": …}]; replaces the built-in pairs.

rules.name: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
rules.description: An UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE in a string literal, SQL.Text, SQL.Add, CommandText, the first argument of ExecSQL, ExecSQLScalar, ExecuteDirect or Execute, or in SQL.Strings/CommandText of the form file. It affects every row of the table; usually the condition was forgotten. The rule assembles the SQL text per query within a routine (Clear and a new Text start over) and substitutes constants and local values. JOIN, TOP, LIMIT and ROWS restrict the rows as well; a WHERE in a subquery or comment does not count. Unknown parts behind the table name (variables, calls at the place of a clause) keep the statement silent; a dynamic table name reports with medium confidence. Silent when the routine passes the SQL on or another routine of the unit adds to it; form file SQL only counts when the unit does not change it. Literals outside SQL properties count only with DELETE or UPDATE in capitals, so message texts stay silent. High confidence, no quick fix; tables that are emptied on purpose go into allowTables.
rules.bad:
qry.SQL.Text := 'DELETE FROM Warenkorb';
qry.ExecSQL;

options.name: allowTables
options.description: Tables that are deliberately emptied or changed completely, with or without schema.

rules.name: Implementation differs from declaration
rules.description: The header in the implementation section has different parameters (count, name, type, const/var/out), a different result type, procedure instead of function or a different calling convention than the declaration in the type (like E2037). With overloads the nearest declaration is compared (parameter count, then types, names and modifiers); if that is not unique, declared-not-implemented and implemented-not-declared report both sides instead. A body may omit the parameter list, the result type and the calling convention. Methods inside {$IF} blocks are skipped; with include files the confidence is medium. Quick fix: align the implementation header with the declaration, or, as the second action, the declaration with the implementation (default values stay in the declaration). Off with refactoring.syncSignatures = false only removes the quick fixes.

rules.name: Interface method missing in the class
rules.description: A class lists an interface but does not implement all of its methods, including those of ancestor interfaces (like E2291). A method of the class with the same name but a different signature is reported at that method (like E2211). Methods inherited from ancestor classes, method resolution clauses (procedure IFoo.Bar = Baz) and properties with implements count; public TObject methods and IInterface methods of TInterfacedObject and similar RTL bases count as well. If the chain of ancestor classes ends at an unknown class or the interface is unknown, the rule stays silent. A method resolution clause for an interface the class does not list is reported too (like E2265). Classes inside {$IF} blocks are skipped. Quick fix: declare the missing methods and create empty bodies (not offered when a header differs).

rules.name: Unit in uses not found
